questions.text: What is a struct in Rust?

answers.text: A user-defined type that groups several related values into one logical unit
A loop with named branches
A synonym for a homogeneous array
Only a constructor function

questions.explanation: A structure is described as a user-defined type for naming and grouping related values.

source.section: Using Structs to Structure Related Data
source.locator: Chapter 5 — Using Structs to Structure Related Data, pp. 112

questions.text: How does a regular structure differ from a tuple in the way its data parts are described?

answers.text: Structure fields have names
A structure cannot store different types
A tuple always has named fields
A structure is not a type

questions.explanation: In a structure, each piece of data is named, so you do not have to rely only on value order.

source.locator: Chapter 5 — Defining and Instantiating Structs, pp. 113

questions.text: When creating a structure instance, must fields appear in the same order as in the definition?

answers.text: No; values are associated with field names
Yes; otherwise the code never compiles
Only for `String` fields
Only in release builds

questions.explanation: The material states that field order does not have to match the definition when creating an instance.

questions.text: When can field-init shorthand be used?

answers.text: When the variable/parameter name matches the field name
Only when the field has type `bool`
Only for the first field
Only in a tuple struct

questions.explanation: When the names match, `email` can be written instead of `email: email`.

questions.text: What does `..user1` mean in an expression that creates a new structure?

answers.text: Take the remaining fields from `user1`
Delete all fields from `user1`
Make all fields public
Create an empty range

questions.explanation: Struct update syntax `..user1` fills unspecified fields with values from `user1`.

questions.text: Why can the original `user1` become unavailable after creating `user2` with `..user1`?

Any `..` syntax always deletes the entire source object
The `active: bool` field does not implement Copy
Structures can never be used twice

questions.text: What is a tuple struct?

answers.text: A structure with a type name but without names for individual fields
An ordinary tuple without its own type
A structure with only one field
A structure whose fields are automatically public

questions.explanation: A tuple struct has a type name and field types, but the fields themselves are unnamed.

answers.text: Each declared structure defines its own type
Because the contained values are different
Because `Color` always contains strings
They are actually the same type

answers.text: The instance on which the method is called
The module name
A random value
Only the static type without an instance

All variants exist simultaneously

Only a numeric constant

questions.explanation: An enumeration defines a type as one of several possible variants.

questions.text: During struct update, which fields can be copied from the source value without moving them? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A `bool` field, because its type implements `Copy`
A `u64` field, because its type implements `Copy`
A `String` field, because all struct fields are copied implicitly
None: struct update always moves the entire source instance as one unit

questions.explanation: Fields of `Copy` types such as `bool` and `u64` are copied. Owning fields such as `String` may be moved.
